newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PM SAYS ECON GROWTH REQUIRES CUTS - AGENCY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PM SAYS ECON GROWTH REQUIRES CUTS - AGENCY.

text.p: Economic growth is now so strong that the government must tighten fiscal policy to ensure a continued and stable growth trend, Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
In an interview with Finnish news agency STT, Lipponen said it was a matter of the business cycle.
"To ensure growth, it is necessary to a certain extent to tighten fiscal policy," the agency quoted him as saying.

The finance ministry's 1998 budget proposal, which put the deficit at about 17 billion markka, down from an earlier projected 21 billion, has sparked criticism from many cabinet ministers and some have said it breached agreements.
Lipponen said he did not approve of the claims that the extra cuts would have come as a surprise, and said he had given hints in an interview in early July about what was to come.

"Economic policy-making is not excegetics, to act on the basis of what the situation was half a year or a year ago. It has to be conducted in time, and this issue is about whether the government takes responsibility for economic policy," STT quoted Lipponen as saying.
